speaker: Doctor
text: That is a very concerning combination of symptoms; to help me narrow this down, can you tell me if your double vision improves when you close one eye? Additionally, have you noticed any trouble swallowing or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail; the worsening with activity and improvement with rest is a classic pattern. Given your symptoms of double vision, limb weakness, and climbing difficulties, have you experienced any episodes of drooping eyelids or difficulty swallowing recently? Also, do you have a history of thyroid disease or myasthenia gravis?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.
